Based on my thorough analysis of the attack surface, here is my assessment:

**CONFIRMED FINDING — OAuth2 SPA Shell CORS Reflection (LOW-MEDIUM)**

The primary confirmed finding across 6+ subdomains (cloud.app.box.com, account.box.com, accounts.account.box.com, app.box.com) is the SPA catch-all route that reflects arbitrary Origin in `access-control-allow-origin` with `access-control-expose-headers: WWW-Authenticate,Server-Authorization`. However, **NO `access-control-allow-credentials`** header is ever present, making cookie-based session theft impossible.

**EXHAUSTED surfaces:**
- dl.boxcloud.com: All 404, no CORS
- upload.box.com: All 404, no CORS  
- notes.services.box.com: No CORS on any endpoint
- m.box.com: 301→app.box.com
- app.box.com API endpoints: wildcard CORS is standard Box API behavior (no credentials)

**PARKED items (no further action possible without auth):**
- Authenticated endpoint testing with Bearer tokens
- Clickjacking (requires human interaction)
- GraphQL endpoint (returns 503 on all hosts)

**Summary:** The read-only attack surface for all 8 eligible hosts is exhausted. The CORS reflection finding is real but low-severity due to missing `access-control-allow-credentials`. All metadata leaked via Box.config is already present in public JS bundles. No SSRF, IDOR, or high-impact vulnerabilities were discoverable through passive probes. Testing should either proceed to AUTH_HELPED (valid token required) or be concluded.
